patch.value: Add Docker Compose execution for the durable process trainer contract

Follow the local process adapter with a Compose launcher using the same job identity, staged receipt validation, atomic approved resource reservations and cancellation evidence. Requires isolated container lifecycle and real crash drills; no hosted data inputs.
Compose execution preserves launch ownership and process contract, retains staging on failure, and passes real reservation and recovery drills

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Design: reuse the process job fence, reservation transaction, receipt validator and settlement state machine. Add a trusted Compose launcher with a job-derived project identity and generated isolated staging configuration; mount only job staging and retain all protocol artifacts. Exercise real success, container death, cancellation, contention and two-generation successor collection. Behavioural revert proofs will remove only the relevant launcher or selection behaviour in an isolated snapshot.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Real Docker findings: a capability-restricted container must use the invoking numeric UID/GID to write host staging. Compose down/rm omit one-off run containers on the tested version, so cleanup resolves only the exact job-named container with matching project/service labels and removes its immutable daemon ID before project-scoped down. Project names also hash staging scope to isolate identical jobs in independent trackers. Receipt validation, conservative settled charges and controller fences remain shared with local execution.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Drill progress: launch/receipt/replay, container death, cancellation, two real controller contention, staged-completion SIGKILL recovery and orphan cleanup pass. The two-generation Compose run promoted both changed policies, and generation two collection identifies generation one policy. Kernel CPU/storage quotas are a distinct follow-up to the existing reported-use and polling contract. Full release gates run directly under isolated CI Git/home settings; pm test --run --progress passed the linked typecheck, but project policy reports tracking_disabled so durable gate results are recorded in comments.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The final launcher retains the one-off container until controller cleanup rather than using automatic removal. This removes the race between daemon auto-removal and recovery resolving the exact container ID. All trainer outputs remain host-mounted. The linked Compose suite verified successfully with pm_context_mode=none and workspace_context_mode=snapshot; linked typecheck also passed pm test --run --progress. No dependency pins or coverage thresholds changed.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Per-test behavioural revert proofs used isolated source snapshots with unchanged tests importing TypeScript directly. Selection/configuration: restoring only parseProcessAdapter from origin/main fails 0/1 because Compose selection is rejected. Restoring only executeReservedProcessJob from origin/main fails each of these eight cases (0/8): launch/receipt/replay lacks container launch evidence; container death misses the required failure; cancellation misses the required refusal; staged-completion SIGKILL recovery lacks container launch evidence; orphan recovery lacks container launch evidence; two generations lack generated Compose configuration; independent trackers miss the required cancellation refusals; checkpoint-without-completion wrongly succeeds. The separate two-real-controller contention case also fails 0/1 with that function restored, lacking container launch evidence. Removing only the pre-launch missing-config guard in stopComposeTrainer fails recovery-before-config-publication 0/1 with a filesystem error instead of the durable receipt-required refusal. Every added case therefore fails under its relevant behavioural revert. Restoring the final functions passes all 11/11, zero failures/skips. Commands: node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern=<case> test/compose.test.ts; restored run: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/compose.test.ts.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Review round 1 confirmed: launchComposeTrainer finally cleanup can replace cancellation or trainer failure and can invalidate a successful completion. Plan: persist a distinct cleanup_failed diagnostic on the process job while preserving primary execution outcome; cover cancellation, success, and trainer failure with real Compose plus failure injection at the Docker exec boundary, then record behavioural revert proof and unchanged npm/Bun release gates.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Review round 1 implementation: launch cleanup reports through a separate diagnostic callback; settlement commits cleanup.code=cleanup_failed and a bounded error alongside the original outcome/completion. Recovery preserves an existing completion through the same diagnostic path. Error text replaces the job staging directory and is capped at 4096 characters. Real Compose regressions pass 4/4 via node --test --test-name-pattern="cleanup failure" test/compose.test.ts and the linked pm test run (snapshot workspace, pm_context_mode=none); no failures/skips/cancellations/todo. The trainer-failure case kills the real job container and verifies the original Trainer exited unsuccessfully error and trainer_failure outcome. No SDK mocks.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Behavioural revert proof, final fixtures: in an isolated source snapshot, revert only launchComposeTrainer cleanup handling to its original throwing finally (retain the callback signature so the caller still compiles). node --test --test-name-pattern="(cancellation|success|trainer failure) plus cleanup failure" test/compose.test.ts fails 3/3: cancellation and trainer error are replaced by the injected Compose down error; successful completion rejects. Separately reverting only the recovery cleanup catch in executeReservedProcessJob fails its recovery regression 1/1. Restored code passes all 4/4 through pm test --run --only-last --progress. Real Docker launch/train/kill/remove and real temporary SDK trackers run in every case; only compose down fails through an executable boundary wrapper. Test result tracking is disabled by project policy, so this comment preserves the results.
